scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C#
scalesUsed.application: Provides the bright, buoyant melodic backbone and the shimmering open-string resonances of the signature guitar riff

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C
scalesUsed.application: Infuses the chorus and transitions with gritty classic-rock swagger via the flatted 7th degree (C natural)
Forms the clean, driving framework for the lead fills and vocal-response phrases

mainProgression.progression: I - II - I6 - II - IV - V
mainProgression.description: An endlessly cyclical glam-rock groove. The opening riff oscillates between D and E major triads with ringing open high B and E strings, creating an addictive suspended chime before resolving through G and A.

sectionProgressions.description: Alan Parker and David Bowie's immortal syncopated riff bouncing between open D bass pedal notes and high ringing strings
Driving 4/4 rock progression punctuated by steady downstroke strums and punchy backbeat accents
Anthemic stadium cadence powered by open cowboy chord voicings and emphatic vocal call-and-response

sectionProgressions.progression: C - G - D - C - G - A
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: bVII - IV - I - bVII - IV - V
sectionProgressions.description: Dramatic modal detour introducing the subtonic C natural chord for pure 1970s rock grit before launching back into the main riff

harmonicFunction: D (I) - Tonic chord anchoring the buoyant, defiant rock groove
E (II) - Secondary dominant / major II chord providing unexpected harmonic lift and bright tension
G (IV) - Subdominant chord creating open harmonic warmth in the verse and chorus climbs
A (V) - Dominant chord delivering the classic turnaround tension pulling back to tonic D
C (bVII) - Borrowed Mixolydian chord in the bridge injecting raw rock rebellious edge

techniques.name: Syncopated Open-String Pedal Riffing
techniques.description: Alternating fretted double stops on the G and B strings against ringing open high E and D pedal tones, generating a lively chiming rhythm with minimal hand movement

notes: Anchor your ring finger lightly on fret 3 of the B string while allowing the open high E string to ring freely
Use a crisp down-up picking motion over strings 1, 2, and 3
Keep the index finger flat to lightly mute the unplayed low E and A strings
Accentuate the syncopated upbeats on beats 2-and and 4-and for authentic glam swagger
sequence: Strike the open D 4th string downbeat
Fret 2 on G string and 3 on B string, strumming crisp eighth-note accents
Shift quickly to open G and fret 2 on B string for the suspended resolution
Maintain relaxed wrist oscillation at 126 BPM
tips: Do not press too hard with the fret hand or you will choke the open ringing high E string
Use a medium 0.73mm to 0.88mm plectrum for crisp treble clarity and flexible strumming attack
Keep your guitar volume slightly backed off to let the tube amp clean up dynamically

techniques.name: Glam-Rock Staccato Chunking
techniques.description: Tight rhythmic palm muting on the lower registers interspersed with sharp percussive chord stabs to drive the verse groove behind the vocal

notes: Apply the fleshy outer edge of the pick-hand palm lightly against the bridge saddles
Execute driving eighth-note downstrokes on the root and fifth strings
Release the palm mute abruptly on beats 2 and 4 to let full triads ring with punch
Dampen strings immediately on upbeat sixteenths with the fret hand
sequence: Palm-mute the D5 power chord downstrokes
Open up the pick hand for the unmuted high D major triad stab
Slide fret-hand shape two frets up to E5 with sharp pick attack
Return to tight muted chugging on the turnaround
tips: Listen to Mick Ronson's early glam production influence for the exact blend of crisp cut and fat midrange
Maintain strict metronomic timing without rushing the upbeat syncopations
Coordinate breath with downbeats to prevent pick-hand tension during extended live performances

sections.name: Intro Signature Glam Riff
sections.description: The immortal opening hook: an unforgettable, chiming six-note arpeggiated motif played on an electric guitar with light tube overdrive and ringing open strings.
notes: Let the open D and high E strings ring throughout each measure
Hit the upbeat accents cleanly with alternate pick strokes
Clean slide into fret 2 on the G string sets the hook in motion
Maintain snappy 126 BPM forward momentum

sections.name: Verse 1 Driving Rhythm
sections.description: Bowie's swaggering vocal delivery backed by punchy open-chord strumming and syncopated rhythmic stops on beats 2 and 4.
notes: Tight palm muting on the downbeats
Accentuate beats 2 and 4 with bright open chord voicings
Crisp release on beat 4-and leaves room for the drum snare smack
Smooth transition between E major and G major cowboy shapes

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Hook
sections.description: 'Rebel Rebel, you've torn your dress' - full open guitar chords ring out behind the iconic lead riff counterpoint.
notes: Big open strumming pattern across all six strings
Rhythm guitar locks in with the bass drum for punchy downbeats
Lead guitar doubles the main riff during vocal pauses
Dynamic crescendo leading into the second verse

sections.name: Bridge Modal Detour
sections.description: Harmonic departure introducing C major and G major, injecting bluesy rock tension before building through an extended A dominant chord.
sections.progression: C - G - D - C - G - A
notes: The flat-VII C chord provides immediate harmonic lift and grit
Heavy downstroke strums build intensity across four measures
Vamp on A dominant with rhythmic sixteenth-note accents
Snap back to the open D intro riff on beat 1

sections.name: Lead Fills & Outro Jam
sections.description: High-energy outro vamp repeating the signature riff while second guitar layers tasteful pentatonic double-stop bends and rhythmic fills.
notes: Add subtle blues bends on fret 5 of the G string (C to C#)
Double stops at frets 7 and 8 on the B and high E strings add sparkle
Keep the groove centered around the snare backbeat
Slow, triumphant studio fadeout

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster or Gibson Les Paul Standard
guitar.pickup: Bridge single-coil or bridge humbucker for cutting upper midrange

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W or Fender Twin Reverb pushed to mild breakup

effects.distortion: Light vintage tube overdrive (Boss OD-1, Ibanez TS808, or cranked Marshall preamp)
effects.other: Analog tape slapback delay (120ms, single repeat)

beginner.title: Open Cowboy Chords & Basic Strumming
steps: Memorize the open D, E, G, and A cowboy chord fingerings
Practice shifting cleanly between D and E without pausing on beat 1
Master the 126 BPM eighth-note strumming rhythm using a light pick

intermediate.title: Mastering the Signature Arpeggiated Riff
steps: Practice fretting the D and E double stops while keeping the high E string ringing
Syncopate the pick hand to nail the upbeats on beats 2 and 4
Incorporate tight palm muting for the verse chunking sections

advanced.title: Lead Phrasing, Double Stops & Full Track Groove
steps: Execute the outro double stops and vocal-response lead licks in time
Balance two-guitar layering in a band context without sonic clutter
Perform the entire 4:34 track at full 126 BPM tempo with authentic swagger

commonMistakes: Accidentally muting the ringing open high E string during the main riff
Rushing the syncopated upbeats instead of sitting in the pocket at 126 BPM
Using too much distortion, which turns the open chord chime into muddy noise
Strumming too aggressively on the verse chunking instead of using controlled palm muting
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Open string arpeggio drill across D, G, B, and high E strings
10 mins: Slow metronome practice of the main 2-bar riff at 90, 110, and 126 BPM
10 mins: Verse-to-chorus rhythm transition drills with dynamic volume changes
10 mins: Outro double-stop fill work with backing track
focusAreas: Open string clarity and fret-hand arch ergonomics
Syncopated pick-hand attack and accent control
Dynamic contrast between rhythm verse muting and soaring chorus chords
metronomeWork: Begin looping the main riff at 85 BPM to ensure absolute note cleanliness
Increase tempo by 5 BPM once 4 error-free cycles are achieved
Set the click to beats 2 and 4 to develop authentic rock groove
